chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Lu's act in Montreal and the pianist who refused to play blues
summary: Danny put a group together around Lu singing blues, but their piano player quit playing blues at Ciro's in Montreal; they try to name him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I just left. So I'm around there. So I hit Broadway now. Now I'm hustling, hustling songs, see. And I'm a rhythm guitar player; I'm not a fast fly guitar player leading in order to be up front. You know, they got them cats got them groups and they're playin'. So I figured I'd do a little thing with my old lady.

So I tried, and we got a little group together, and we couldn't get nobody to cooperate 'cause she's singin' blues -- and they look at you after a while. You know, I had two or three cats, and one of them told me... I booked them, and we played the first night -- and he was one of them Muslims, I can't think of his name. A piano player... And we washed him, washed his clothes, fed him, gave him some money and everything. And we're going to Montreal. We

go to Montreal, to Ciro's, and when we get there, it's good, he's playing, she's goin' over great. The second night we hit, and after we played the second note, he said, "Man, I ain't playin' no more Blues." No, we started off; I hit the introduction...
A little piano player. He works with Hawkins' little brother... What's that boy's name, a tenor player from Kansas City who got hurt...
He used to work with Basie.
Buddy Tate. This piano player played later with Buddy Tate on 125th Street. They worked on that gig for years -- between Lenox and Fifth. Remember that club down there?
